messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm proposing a compactification of the console ingest schema to cut per-route telemetry storage. Need a quick sync on quotas, routing, and dashboard fallbacks.

sam: Short q — which fields are we moving or compacting? need clarity for query fallbacks.

maria: Plan sketch: move high-cardinality route_attrs map into a separate denorm table called route_attr_keys and keep a compact route_signatures blob for the console hot-path. Dual-write new schema alongside existing for 2w. Backfill hourly aggregates for >30d windows to avoid massive replay.

ben: Concern — alerting drilldowns depend on route_attrs. If we compact, dashboards that drill to attr-level will break for older windows. UX idea: show a banner "expanded attrs unavailable for this time window" and link to aggregated breakdown. @elaine?

elaine: Agree on the banner. Also add provenance metadata (live_vs_aggregated) per timeseries and expose attr_resolution_version in the telemetry contract so callers can opt into the heavier join when needed.

kai: @maria what's the migration window and backfill throughput? need to avoid quota calc spikes and coordinate with billing exports.

maria: Canary plan: 10% tenants weekend canary -> 48h monitoring -> ramp if healthy. Backfill will be an incremental hourly job writing denorm rows; estimated 18h per region for a 90d horizon but we'll throttle to keep DB iowait and quota usage low.

ben: Routing note: read-adapter should prefer the compact index and only fallback to legacy storage if a join is required. That keeps p99 down. We'll gate with a feature flag.

sam: Feature flag + read-adapter makes sense. Also propose read-path exposes meta.attr_status so programmatic clients can detect full vs partial attrs and avoid 202-style behavior.

elaine: Agreed — hide 202s. API returns { meta: { attr_status: "partial|complete" } } so SDKs can surface the banner and adjust UI behavior.

maria: Finalized for now: dual-write -> read-adapter prefers new table -> UI shows "partial attrs" when needed -> backfill -> switch default read to new table after 2w if no regressions. I will author a migration runbook.

kai: Quota calc impact: if read-adapter adds joins, route those queries to a cached denorm path. Add an observability dashboard for quota p95/p99 on canary tenants and an alert for >15% latency regression.

ben: +1 Also add an alert for cost-per-query on telemetry endpoints.

elaine: Who owns the backfill runbook and oncall play for the migration? Ops or eng-platform?

maria: I'll own the runbook; ops will run heavy lifting. Draft runbook link (stub): https://ourwiki.local/migrations/console-compactify

sam: Add rollback steps: stop dual-write, revert read-adapter config, and a controlled replay to revert denorm rows if abort. DB migrations must use CONCURRENT index builds and preflight index time estimates.

maria: Rollback checklist: 1) pause backfill 2) switch read-adapter to legacy 3) mark migration aborted in audit log 4) cleanup indexes as needed. We'll enforce CONCURRENT index creation and run preflight queries to estimate time.

kai: Can we aim for next Friday 02:00 UTC canary? I'll reserve the maintenance window and monitor rotation.

maria: Yes — scheduling for next Friday 02:00 UTC. I'll post a detailed checklist in #eng-platform later today.

ben: Small nit — keep billing exports on legacy canonical fields until billing confirms parity. Don't surprise billing.

elaine: I'll loop in billing (cc @tom) to validate parity and sign-off on switching exports.

deploy-bot: Feature flag created: console.compactify.v1 (id: ff-789) — created by maria.

maria: Thanks all — I'll follow up with a short RFC including DDLs, sample queries, and cost estimates.
